spec_issues: Held-out: 4,400 rows of BTZSC (22 datasets x 200), each rescaled from a uniform-probability floor to 1.0 (tests/task/task.yaml:42-67). The 500 shipped rows are DBpedia-14 test rows and may only be used to check the server.

The upstream-source rule is uneven. DATA_POLICY.md bans the BTZSC sources and their 'mirrors, subsets or derivatives', and lists other-name derivatives only for Rotten Tomatoes (SST/MR/subj) and TrueTeacher (CNN/DM, FactCC, FRANK, SummEval). SBF sources: Social Bias Frames is built partly from posts in Davidson et al. 2017 (tdavidson/hate_speech_offensive), Founta 2018, Waseem & Hovy 2016 and Stormfront (de Gibert 2018, hate_speech18). DATA_POLICY.md:10 bans 'Social Bias Frames' and its 'mirrors, subsets or derivatives' but names no upstream sources for it, while it does name TrueTeacher's upstream CNN/DailyMail (DATA_POLICY.md:28-33). The same reading problem applies to MASSIVE (built from SLURP/HWU64) and Yelp (DynaSent). Agents split on it. Opus 2bb9rl and 3jhxni excluded these upstream corpora explicitly (2bb9rl [15]: 'Banned (plus upstream sources): SLURP/HWU64 (MASSIVE source), Davidson/Founta/Waseem/Gab/Stormfront (SBF sources)'). Fable 1w83ln [23] ('== davidson: +3000'), Fable 42xw3e [50], Opus 1j4hzb [98] ('hate_speech_offensive toxicity 3 8000'), DeepSeek 58tjfz and Muse 1ftq4w trained on Davidson and/or hate_speech18. The reviewer passed all of them, consistently across models, because review.py:13-27 lists only the named derivatives.

Fable 42xw3e also trained on allenai/prosocial-dialog ([50] source list; 'prosocial' appears in its in-domain dev at [108]). I believe ProsocialDialog seeds its contexts partly from the Social Bias Inference Corpus. That would make it a derivative of SBF, which the rule names explicitly. The trajectory does not show its card, so I cannot confirm this from public data.

Fable 4zb5b5 was zeroed for FinanceInc/auditor_sentiment, a re-host of Financial PhraseBank. The name hides the source, and no other-name list covers it. The reviewer inferred it from row counts (3,877 + 969 = 4,846 = FPB sentences_50agree). The call is right under 'mirrors', but an agent could not easily know.
verifier_issues: Score: mean over 22 datasets of normalised macro-F1 x (1 - top-label ECE, 15 bins), each from its own uniform floor. Binary datasets have floors around 0.51-0.52 (amazonpolarity, imdb, rottentomatoes, yelp, wikitoxic), so their normalisation roughly doubles noise. With 200 rows per dataset, per-dataset normalised SE is about 5-8 points, and the 22-dataset mean has an SE of about 1.3-1.5 points.
Probabilities must sum to 1 within 1e-6, and the batch has an 88 s deadline for 4,400 docs. No trial failed a gate in grading.

Per-dataset scores on the grade pages show no visible gain from SBF-source training. The SBF mean normalised score (intent, offensive, sex) is 42.1 for Fable 1w83ln, 43.9 for Fable 42xw3e and 42.9 for Opus 1j4hzb, all Davidson users. It is 42.6 for Opus 3jhxni, 32.7 for Opus 2bb9rl and 43.1 for Astra 66jjjy, which did not use Davidson.
task_level.noise: Overall SE is about 1.3-1.5 points. At $10, Fable 42xw3e (59.6), Opus 2bb9rl (59.3) and Gemini 2pnpy0 (58.6) are a three-way tie within noise. At $200, Fable 1w83ln (62.1) leads Opus 3jhxni (59.0) by about 2 SE. At $50, Opus 1j4hzb (57.7) beats Gemini 1bf19e (54.8). The Fable $50 zero is a review fail. Wallet order is flat or non-monotone for every model: Opus 59.3/57.7/59.0, Gemini 58.6/54.8/37.7, Muse 48.6/16.0/37.1. Extra money did not help.
task_level.elicitation: Astra used only 0.65-1.28 agent hours of 12, and 66jjjy trained a rank-8 LoRA for 300 steps. Muse 4tvmr8 (16.0) trained a ModernBERT-base bi-encoder. The four Qwen3-4B-Instruct LoRA runs that score highest (Fable, Opus, Gemini 2pnpy0) all came from frontier-lab harnesses at high effort. Gemini runs are dated 2026-10-14, after release; no trial accessed the HF tasks dataset or repo. Muse 5gai5b mentions frontier_ml only in the shipped manifest.
task_level.epoch_rationale: The one review fail (Fable 4zb5b5, Financial PhraseBank mirror) is correct, and no infrastructure zero occurred. The SBF upstream-source rule is ambiguous. Under a strict reading, Davidson and Stormfront training would void Fable's wins at $10 and $200 and Opus's at $50, handing them to Opus 2bb9rl (59.3), Opus 3jhxni (59.0) and Gemini 1bf19e (54.8). Under the written rule, which the reviewer applied, the winners stand. The $10 winner also turns on whether ProsocialDialog counts as an SBF derivative (Fable 42xw3e), which I cannot settle from public data. Per-dataset scores show no measurable benefit from that data.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: No trial gamed the scorer. The top results are standard: Qwen3-4B-Instruct (or Qwen2.5-3B) with LoRA plus a listwise or pointer label head, trained on large multi-task mixtures of public classification train splits with LLM-paraphrased label descriptions, NLI data and synthetic tasks, then temperature-calibrated on held-out train rows. Fable, Opus and Gemini all reach 58-62. NLI cross-encoders and bi-encoders (DeepSeek, Muse, Astra 18lqgv/2pngu5) plateau at 37-48. The main risk in this task is data provenance: avoiding mirrors and derivatives of 22 well-known datasets inside large HF mixtures.

trials.approach: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 with LoRA (r=32) and a bilinear pointer head trained on about 104k multi-task examples from about 50 public train splits plus DeepSeek-generated synthetic tasks. Temperature T=1.3 fitted on held-out train datasets.

SBF sources: Social Bias Frames is built partly from posts in Davidson et al. 2017 (tdavidson/hate_speech_offensive), Founta 2018, Waseem & Hovy 2016 and Stormfront (de Gibert 2018, hate_speech18). DATA_POLICY.md:10 bans 'Social Bias Frames' and its 'mirrors, subsets or derivatives' but names no upstream sources for it, while it does name TrueTeacher's upstream CNN/DailyMail (DATA_POLICY.md:28-33). ProsocialDialog may derive from SBIC, which would make it an explicitly banned 'derivative'. This cannot be confirmed from the trajectory, hence unclear.
SBF normalised mean 43.9 against 32.7 for Opus 2bb9rl: about +1.5 overall points from SBF datasets, in a 0.3-point win at $10.
